paper.title: Learning to Detect an Odd Restless Markov Arm with a Trembling Hand

settings.name_in_paper: Odd arm identification in a restless multi-armed bandit with Markov arms, unknown TPMs, trembling hand
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Restless Markov arms (markovian environment) are out of scope from ontology v0.5.
unmapped: each arm is an ergodic finite-state Markov chain; one odd arm has TPM P1, all others share TPM P2 != P1, both unknown
trembling hand: intended arm sampled w.p. 1-eta, otherwise a uniformly random arm (eta > 0); actual arm observed
goal: identify the odd arm index with error probability <= epsilon uniformly over all configurations, minimising expected stopping time
settings.definition_quote: Consider a multi-armed bandit with $K\geq 3$ arms ... For each $a\in \mathcal{A}$, consider a discrete-time Markov process $\{X_t^a:t\geq 0\}$ associated with arm $a$ that is time-homogeneous, ergodic and takes values in a common finite set $\mathcal{S}$. ... Let the TPM of one of the arms (the {\em odd} arm) be $P_1$, and that of each non-odd arm be $P_2$, where $P_2\neq P_1$. ... A decision entity that knows neither $P_1$ nor $P_2$ wishes to find the odd arm index as quickly as possible while keeping the probability of its decision error small.

algorithms.name: Policy pi*(L, delta) (certainty equivalence with ML estimates and modified GLR stopping)

symbols.R_star: max-min constant R*(h,P1,P2): sup over SRS policies of inf over alternative configurations of the occupancy-weighted KL divergences of delay-dependent TPM rows

conditions: policy class Pi(epsilon): error probability <= epsilon for all arms configurations

source.label: prop:lower_bound
source.quote: Under the arms configuration $C=(h, P_1, P_2)$, \liminf_{\epsilon\downarrow 0}\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\epsilon)}\frac{E^\pi[\tau(\pi)| C]}{\log(1/\epsilon)}\geq \frac{1}{R^*(h,P_1,P_2)}

results.notes: Restated as the lower bound part of Theorem 1. Holds for all configurations.

symbols.L_thr: threshold parameter L of the policy (stop when M >= log((K-1)L))

conditions: Assumption 2 (TPM regularity: nonzero entries of all powers >= eps_bar*)
tuning: L = 1/epsilon gives pi*(L,delta) in Pi(epsilon) for all delta > 0

source.label: prop:policy_satisfies_desried_error_probability
source.quote: Fix an error probability $\epsilon>0$. If $L=1/\epsilon$, then $\pi^{\star}(L,\delta)\in\Pi(\epsilon)$ for all $\delta>0$.

results.notes: Proof shows error probability <= 1/L; probability field set to high_probability as the closest fit for an error-probability guarantee.

symbols.L_thr: threshold parameter L of the policy
symbols.delta_alg: near-optimality slack delta of the delta-optimal sampling rule

source.label: prop:almost_sure_upper_bound_for_policy
source.quote: Suppose that $C=(h, P_1, P_2)$ is the underlying arms configuration. For all $\delta>0$, the stopping time of policy $\pi^\star(L,\delta)$ satisfies \limsup_{L\to\infty} \frac{\tau(\pi^\star(L,\delta))}{\log L} \leq \frac{(1+\delta)^2}{R^*(h, P_1, P_2)} almost surely.

symbols.L_thr: threshold parameter L (L = 1/epsilon for error probability epsilon)

source.label: prop:upper_bound
source.quote: Fix $\delta>0$. Under the arms configuration $C=(h, P_1, P_2)$, the expected stopping time of the policy $\pi=\pi^{\star}(L,\delta)$ satisfies \limsup_{L \to \infty} \frac{E^\pi[\tau(\pi)|C]}{\log L} \leq \frac{(1+\delta)^2}{R^*(h, P_1, P_2)}.

results.notes: With L=1/epsilon this gives (1+delta)^2 log(1/epsilon)/R* asymptotically.

source.label: prop:main_result
source.quote: Further, under Assumption 1 and Assumption 2, the policy $\pi^\star(L, \delta)$ satisfies the asymptotic upper bound \limsup_{\delta\downarrow 0} \limsup_{L\to\infty}\frac{E^{\pi^\star(L, \delta)}[\tau(\pi^\star(L, \delta))|C]}{\log L}\leq \frac{1}{R^*(h, P_1, P_2)}. Under these assumptions, we therefore have \lim_{\epsilon\downarrow 0}\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\epsilon)}\frac{E^\pi[\tau(\pi)|C]}{\log(1/\epsilon)}=...=\frac{1}{R^*(h, P_1, P_2)}.

results.notes: Theorem 1 also restates the lower bound of Proposition 1 (recorded as r1) and concludes matching asymptotic optimality under the assumptions.
